entry_state: Two product-region allocations preserve all numeric margins but imply different conditional sales losses. Named subsidiaries, ownership paths, sellers, manufacturers, tax residences and functional currencies require different evidence. Legal allegations, decisions, remedies and management loss assessments also remain distinct; the next section begins the problem of later disclosures about earlier periods.
exit_state: Later comparative segment expenses can reveal old-period detail without changing its transactions or proving earlier availability. Indemnities, defense, settlement and insurance require separate facts. Regulation, demand, supply interruption and recovery constrain different operating paths; none is identified by a common haircut to a reported balance.
findings: The later Americas expense disclosure reconciles to the earlier reported operating income. Original and later labels, source identities and availability evidence remain separate; retrospective presentation is not interpreted as a correction journal.
No-material-change wording is preserved with its subject and qualifier. It is not upgraded to equality of all estimates, amounts, policies or risks.

Indemnification runs from a third-party claim to a possible Apple obligation. Defense expense can persist despite a successful defense, and insurance requires its own coverage and recognition facts before any offset.
Regulatory procedures are not evidence of actual compliance. A later risk-topic addition does not date a new operative rule, and a paragraph split does not measure increased exposure.

The demand/supply comparison identifies distinct responses and recovery dates. Its assumed alternative supplier needs capacity and terms; ending an interruption does not instantly restore production. No new confirmed defect.
